title: Sliding-window slot allocator and decay-aware restore policy for tiled KV pages
creator: Ava Patel
description: Background: Paged attention uses tiled KV pages to keep memory usage low on large-context requests, but we continue to see tail latency spikes and fragmentation on multi-tenant hosts where short lived spans repeatedly allocate tiny fragments. Motivation: implement a sliding-window slot allocator to prefer temporally local allocations and a decay-aware restore policy that biases restoration/rehydration decisions toward recently accessed tiles. Goal: reduce fragmentation and restore-induced stalls while keeping steady-state hit-rate and not regressing median/99th token latency. Scope: allocator + restore policy + lightweight simulator + runtime integration + benchmarks. Out of scope: global cross-node migration, tenant preemption policies. Deliverables: design doc, simulator results, runtime feature flag, gated rollout, dashboard metrics and alerting. Expected impact: 6-12% reduction in median token decode latency for workloads with interleaved short and long conversations; 20-40% reduction in KV restore stalls in our internal bench-suites that simulate session churn.
acceptance_criteria: Allocator exposes sliding-window tunables (window_ms, stripe_count, hot_threshold) and composes with existing residency pool without allocator-level global locks
Restore policy implements decay score and admission threshold; when decay_score < threshold, restore should be deprioritized and scheduled during soft-warmup windows
Simulator shows at least 8% improvement in measured restore stalls vs baseline on churny session mix (internal workload: chat-churn-v3)
No >5% regression in median or 95th token latency on synthetic steady streams (steady-stream-v2) when feature flag enabled
End-to-end integration covered by unit tests, integration test that replays production traces, and a canary rollout plan with rollback criteria

notes: Design trade-offs: sliding-window favors temporal locality but can starve rarely-used longer sequences; decay-aware restore mitigates by promoting low-decay items during background warmup windows.
Kernel interaction: allocator includes hints to kernel-selector so co-located tiles likely to use same fused-attention kernel lowering cross-page copy cost.
Operational: provide a fast-path that bypasses sliding-window for pinned pages (e.g., deduplicated instruction prompts) to avoid unnecessary reshuffles.
Testing: add fuzz traces that alternate tiny chat messages and long docs to stress fragmentation and validate that allocator recovers within 30s window.
Security & compliance: no customer data exfil changes; feature flag scoped to runtime; security review not required for initial rollout
